newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: Volatility was the South African rand's middle name on Friday.
By the time it had finished being shunted and shafted by a broad front of speculators and corporates, it had chiseled a haphazard-looking arc on the charts.

After initially benefitting from long liquidations out of New York and London overnight -- which helped the rand to a day's strongest level of 4.66 -- the rand was attacked by large dollar buy order out of London which dealers said was speculative.
The ensuing assault pummelled the currency down to the 4.70 level by 0930 GMT, where it succumbed to profit-taking as the dollar gave up an earlier attempt at building a base above 1.87 marks.
"London was playing with the market today," a senior trader said. "They bought it up this morning and tried to sell it down this afternoon...trying to create a bit of volatility."
"We also had a couple of importers in at all different levels," he added.
Another trader said she had seen exporter interest at the higher levels as well.
"We saw good volumes from our corporates. It's been quite volatile all day, but all its really been doing is tracking dollar," she said.
Early in the European day, the dollar probed above the 1.8750 level to touch an intraday high of 1.8764, but fell prey to profit-takers in early New York dealings to last trade at 1.8525/28.
It also weakened to 116 yen from around 118.50 overnight.
The dollar's retreat meant the rand did not fare well against both the mark and yen. It was last trading at 0.3966/3969 from 0.4003/4008 and at 24.8394/8768 yen from 25.2294/2669.
Cable's slump, however yielded gains for the rand against sterling. The cross rate last traded at a fresh eight-week high of 7.3505/3599 from 7.4209/4303.
Dealers said that next week, the rand/dollar's direction would continue to be dictated by the dollar's movements, but did not expect it to move out of its newfound 4.66 to 4.71 range.
